source_bound_facts: Falling slugs are advanced first using equation 19, preserving slug length under the balanced-capillary-force assumption.
Slugs that reach groundwater fronts are merged with the groundwater front and raise its capillary extent by the transferred slug length in that bin.
In the subsequent capillary-relaxation step, slug water in bins to the right that is deeper than slugs to the left is geometrically clipped and moved as far left as possible.
The source states that this process is inherently mass conservative when implemented correctly.
Capillary relaxation at the leading edge produces a sharp bottom front.

blocking_ambiguities: Exact clipping coordinate rule when several left bins can receive water.
Exact event order when multiple disconnected slug intervals overlap in depth.
Exact receiver-capacity rule and whether transfer cascades across more than one bin in one relaxation event.
Exact handling of simultaneous groundwater contact and capillary-relaxation candidates.
Exact linked-list mutation/merge order needed to determine whether multiple slugs per bin can persist.
architecture_binding: Do not approximate geometric clipping by deleting or numerically clipping volume; mass must move to an explicit owner.
Do not assume one slug per bin until M2WC70 data structures and event rules prove that bound.
Any trial relaxation must operate transactionally on a trial copy and commit only after exact volume closure.
Falling-slug relaxation remains separate from the already qualified infiltration/groundwater front-coordinate sorting gate B2B.
